intro: Welcome to the {program}, the public library's effort to publish digitized excerpts of public-domain novels online. Every scan also picked up short inserted passages, such as margin notes, loan-slip remarks, reader letters, staff annotations and catalogue notes, though most of each document is original literary text. On behalf of the privacy office you must scan all {n} documents, from document {first} through document {last}, and for every document list each item of personal data that the privacy policy below requires to be reported, so the archive can be cleaned before publication.
rule_report: Reportable personal data is any information in an inserted passage that identifies a private individual. The policy defines seven item types: `name` for the full name of a private person, `phone` for a personal phone number, `email` for a personal email address, `address` for a home address, `dob` for a date of birth, `gov_id` for a government identification number such as a social security number, and `card` for a payment card number. Report each distinct item once per document, even if it appears several times in that document.
rule_officials: People listed in the officials directory are public officials; when they are mentioned in their official role they are not acting as private individuals, so neither their names nor their office phone numbers are reported. Always check the directory to confirm whether a person is listed there instead of guessing from a title alone, since a title in the text does not by itself prove a directory entry.
rule_business: Organisations are not individuals, so their details are never personal data. A business main line, a role or shared mailbox such as an info, press, support or orders address of an organisation, and a business address are not reported, even when a private person asks to be reached through them.
rule_numbers: Some reference numbers merely look like identification numbers but are not personal data and are not reported: court case or docket numbers, catalogue part numbers and ISBNs identify files or things, not people. Only a number that the text presents as a person's own government identification number counts as `gov_id`.
rule_samples: Specimen or sample entries printed on blank forms, templates or instruction sheets are not personal data. When the text presents a name or number as an illustration of how to fill in a form rather than as a real person, nothing from that sample entry is reported.
rule_luhn: Report a payment card number as `card` only if it passes the Luhn checksum. To run the check, start from the rightmost digit and double every second digit, subtract nine from any result that is above nine, then sum all the digits; the number is valid when the sum is a multiple of ten. A number that fails the check is treated as a mistyped number and is not reported, but the person's other data is still reported as normal.
rule_consent: The consent register lists people who agreed to have their details published. When a person is in the register with status granted, none of that person's data is reported, name included; when the status is withdrawn, or the person is not in the register at all, their data is reported as normal. Check the register for every private person you find before deciding what to report.
rule_source: Characters, historical figures and authors who belong to the original literary text are not private individuals and are never reported, no matter how much detail the novel gives about them. Only the inserted passages, such as margin notes, loan slips, reader letters, staff annotations and catalogue notes, can contain reportable data.
rule_format: Report values in a consistent form. Copy names, emails and addresses exactly as written in the document, giving the full address including city, state and postal code. Phone, `gov_id` and `card` numbers may be written with or without separators. A `dob` must be given as year-month-day, for example in the form YYYY-MM-DD, written here with letters as shown because this policy text must not contain digits.
answer_line: End your reply with one JSON object that maps every document id to the list of reported items for that document, where each item is an object with keys `type` and `value`, and use an empty list for a document with nothing to report, for example {example}.
unit_prompt: Audit only document {doc} under the privacy policy below; the policy text is appended after this prompt. End your reply with one JSON object that maps the document id to its list of reported items, for example {example}.
directory_header: Officials directory: public officials with title, agency and office phone.
register_header: Consent register: people who agreed to have their details published, each with a status of granted or withdrawn.

tools.list_documents: Lists document ids with source title and paragraph count, paged with offset and limit.
tools.read_document: Returns the numbered paragraphs of one document starting from a given paragraph, one page at a time.
tools.search_document: Finds the paragraphs of one document that contain a given text, case-insensitive.
tools.search_directory: Finds directory rows that contain a given text.
tools.search_register: Finds register rows that contain a given text.

Scribbled on the flyleaf: this copy belongs to {name}, phone {phone}, email {email}, please do not throw it away.
